prompt.context: Your client, Salford Breweries, is a medium sized brewer who has recently experienced sales growth in the Chinese market. While this is excellent news, Salford Breweries is facing difficulty growing in a profitable manner. The CEO of Salford Breweries has been instructed by the board to improve the company's net profit by 10% in 2019. She has asked for your help in achieving this target.
prompt.question: How should Salford Breweries achieve a 10% improvement in net profit in 2019?

clarifying_info.q: What was revenue and net profit margin in 2018?
clarifying_info.a: Revenue in 2018 was £220 million, and the net profit margin was 50%.

clarifying_info.q: Where are Salford Breweries' production facilities located?
clarifying_info.a: The client currently has three breweries, all of which are in the United Kingdom.

clarifying_info.q: What is the sales volume breakdown?
clarifying_info.a: Sales in China is currently 360,000 hectolitres (hL), and 1.1M hL for the whole business (1 hL = 100L).

clarifying_info.q: Which markets does Salford Breweries operate in?
clarifying_info.a: Salford Breweries currently only sells to the China and United Kingdom markets.

clarifying_info.q: What products does Salford Breweries sell?
clarifying_info.a: Salford Breweries sells a Lager, an IPA, and a Wheat Beer. The IPA became their best-seller in 2017.

exhibits.title: Variable Costs per Hectolitre by Beer Type and Market
exhibits.shows: A table comparing UK variable cost per hL versus China variable cost per hL for each beer type (IPA, Lager, Wheat Beer), along with China demand volumes and notes about a potential China brewery investment.
exhibits.data: IPA: UK VC £85/hL, China VC £45/hL, China Demand 350,000 hL; Lager: UK VC £75/hL, China VC £40/hL, China Demand 0 hL; Wheat Beer: UK VC £105/hL, China VC £75/hL, China Demand 10,000 hL; Note: Opening a production facility in China requires £5M upfront for 500,000 hL capacity (Lager + IPA capability); Wheat Beer capability costs an additional £5M; Fixed costs £4M per annum; UK VC includes logistics costs to China.

exhibits.title: China Sales Demand by Beer Type
exhibits.shows: A chart or table showing the breakdown of Salford Breweries' current China sales volumes by beer type.
exhibits.data: IPA: 350,000 hL; Lager: 0 hL; Wheat Beer: 10,000 hL; Total China: 360,000 hL

exhibits.title: Brewery Capacity, Capability, and Fixed Costs
exhibits.shows: A table listing each brewery (Sheffield, Manchester, Hackney, and estimated China) with production capability by beer type, capex required to add capability, and fixed costs per annum.
exhibits.data: Sheffield: Lager capability exists, IPA capex £1M, Wheat Beer capex £10M, Fixed Cost £5M/yr; Manchester: Lager capability exists, IPA capability exists, Fixed Cost £7.5M/yr; Hackney: Wheat Beer capability exists, Fixed Cost £2.7M/yr; China (Estimate): Lager capex £5M (£0 if IPA capability exists), IPA capex £5M, Wheat Beer capex £5M, Fixed Cost £4M/yr

framework: Revenue: Quantity sold (volume by market and SKU) x Revenue per unit (price per hL by SKU)
Variable Costs: Production cost per unit by brewery and SKU; Logistics/export costs to China
Fixed Costs: Brewery fixed costs by facility; Administrative and operational overhead
Capabilities & Risks: Export/import capability from UK to China; Chinese division management (sales, marketing); Regulatory requirements to operate in China

questions.prompt: Calculate the 2019 profit target and the required cost reduction.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate 2018 profit, then apply 10% improvement to find the target. Revenues are assumed flat at £220M. 2018 Profit = £220M x 50% = £110M. 2019 target = £110M x 1.10 = £121M. Cost reduction required = £121M - £110M = £11M.

math.setup: 2018 Profit = Revenue x Margin = £220M x 50%. 2019 Profit Target = 2018 Profit x 110%. Cost Reduction Target = 2019 Profit Target - 2018 Profit.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, evaluate whether Salford Breweries should open a brewery in China, and calculate the net cost impact.
questions.guidance: Candidate should evaluate each beer type separately. IPA: VC saving = (£85 - £45) x 350,000 = £14M; less fixed costs £4M/yr; less capex £5M one-time. Net benefit = £14M - £4M - £5M = £5M. Lager has no China demand so no benefit. Wheat Beer: VC saving = (£105 - £75) x 10,000 = £300K; but adding Wheat Beer capability costs £5M; Net impact = £300K - £5M = -£4.7M (do not proceed). Only IPA should be produced in China. Total net cost saving = £5M, which does NOT meet the £11M target.

math.setup: For each beer type: VC Saving = (UK VC - China VC) x China Demand. Net Cost Impact = VC Saving - Annual Fixed Cost Allocation - One-time Investment.
steps: IPA net impact = £14M - £4M fixed costs - £5M investment = £5,000,000 (Proceed)
Wheat Beer net impact = £300K - £5M Wheat Beer capability = -£4,700,000 (Do not proceed)
Total net saving from China brewery (IPA only) = £5M
math.answer: Opening a China brewery for IPA only saves £5M net; this is insufficient to meet the £11M target.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, identify further cost reduction opportunities by rationalizing the UK brewery network, and calculate the total benefit.
questions.guidance: With IPA production moving to China (350,000 hL), Manchester brewery loses volume. Manchester currently produces IPA and Lager. Post-China transition, Manchester capacity utilized drops from 650,000 hL to 300,000 hL. Sheffield can absorb remaining UK IPA volume if £1M capex is spent on IPA capability. Closing Manchester saves £7.5M fixed costs per year, offset by £1M capex to add IPA at Sheffield. Net benefit of Manchester closure = £7.5M - £1M = £6.5M. Total benefit = £5M (China brewery) + £6.5M (Manchester closure) = £11.5M, which exceeds the £11M target.

math.setup: Brewery rationalization: Fixed cost saving from closure less capex required to transfer capability to remaining breweries.
steps: China brewery absorbs 350,000 hL IPA from Chinese demand
Manchester post-transition utilization: 650,000 - 350,000 = 300,000 hL (IPA moved to China)
Manchester can be closed; IPA capability added to Sheffield at £1M capex
Net benefit of Manchester closure = £7.5M fixed costs saved - £1M IPA capex at Sheffield = £6.5M
math.answer: Closing Manchester and adding IPA capability at Sheffield yields £6.5M additional saving. Combined with £5M from China brewery, total saving = £11.5M, exceeding the £11M target.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks do you foresee regarding this change to Salford Breweries' production network?

categories.name: Operational
ideas: Product quality risk when commissioning the new Chinese brewery
Risk of production delays or inefficiencies during scale-up of Chinese operations

categories.name: Financial
ideas: Accuracy of fixed and variable cost estimates for the new Chinese brewery
Potential remediation and closure costs of Manchester brewery, including staff redundancies

categories.name: Public Relations and Regulatory
ideas: Union and labour force reaction to Manchester brewery closure
Chinese consumer perception of locally-produced versus UK-imported beer
Regulatory requirements: may a joint venture be required to operate a brewery in China?

recommendation: Salford Breweries should open a brewery in China with capability to produce IPA and Lager, but should not add Wheat Beer capability as it is not cost optimal given current China demand.
Salford Breweries should close their existing Manchester brewery and invest £1M to add IPA production capability at the Sheffield brewery.
These two changes deliver a combined cost saving of £11.5M, which exceeds the CEO's 2019 profit improvement target of £11M.
risks: Operational risk: ensuring product quality and efficient scale-up of the new Chinese brewery.
Financial risk: actual variable and fixed costs may differ from estimates, affecting the projected saving.
Public relations risk: closing the Manchester brewery may trigger negative union reactions and media coverage.
Regulatory risk: operating a brewery in China may require a local joint venture partner.
next_steps: Determine the feasibility and timeline for opening a brewery in China and scaling IPA production to 350,000 hL.
Quantify the commercial opportunity to introduce Salford Breweries' Lager into the Chinese market.
Develop a Manchester closure plan including staff transition, remediation costs, and communications strategy.
